Every coming is so called when truth flows into thought from the Word.

4713. **And the peace of the flock**, which signifies how it was with those who learn, or the Church, is evident from the signification of "peace," as being how a matter stands, as mentioned just above in n. 4712; and from the signification of "flock," as being those who learn; for the shepherd or the one pasturing is he who teaches and leads to the good of charity, and the flock is those who learn and are led, see n. 343; thus it also signifies the Church.

4714. **And bring me back word**, which signifies knowledge, is evident from the signification of "bringing back word," as being to report how the matter stands, thus knowledge.

4715. **And he sent him out of the valley of Hebron**, which signifies from the Divine Natural and Sensual, is evident from the signification of being "sent," as being to proceed and to teach, see n. 4710; from the signification of "valley," as being those things which are below, see n. 1723, 3417; and from the signification of "Hebron," as being the Lord’s Church as to good, see n. 2909. Thus, these words signify that he would teach those things which are lower in the Church, and this because they would not grasp the higher things. For one who teaches faith and not charity can never perceive the higher or interior things of the Church; for he has nothing to lead him, and nothing to dictate whether this is of faith or whether this is true. But if he teaches charity, then he possesses good; this is a dictate to him and leads him, for all truth is from good and deals with good, or what is the same, all that belongs to faith is from charity and deals with charity. Everyone can know from natural light alone that everything in doctrine looks toward life. That these words signify "from the Divine Natural and Sensual" is the higher sense; for the things that are lower in the Church are said to be from the Divine Natural and Sensual of the Lord—not that these are lower in the Lord, for in the Lord and in His Divine Human everything is Infinite, for He is <term>Jehovah</term> as to both Essences, see n. 2156, 2329, 2921, 3023—but because it is so with man. For those who are sensual men perceive the things that are in the Lord and from the Lord sensually, and those who are natural men perceive them naturally; it is spoken of in this way according to the quality of those who receive it. But those who are celestial men, and thus truly rational, perceive interior things; it is said of them that they are taught from the Divine Rational of the Lord. This is the higher sense, as stated, which is signified by those words. That a "valley" signifies the lower things of the Church can be seen from other places in the Word; as in Isaiah: *“The prophecy of the valley of vision; what is it to you here, that you have all gone up to the rooftops: a day of tumult, and of treading down, and of perplexity to the Lord Jehovih Zebaoth, in the Valley of vision,”* XXII: 1, 5; the "valley of vision" stands for fantasies about spiritual things from sensual things, thus from lower things. In the same: *“The choice of your valleys were filled with chariots, and the horsemen placed themselves at the gate,”* XXII: 7; the "choice of valleys" stands for goods and truths in the natural or external man. In the same: *“The voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare the way of Jehovah, make straight in the desert a path for our God, every valley shall be exalted,”* XL: 3, 4; "valley" stands for the humble.
